summary: A duet with Violette Wautier framed around the emotional vulnerability of that time of the month, and the comment section reads as a support thread rather than a music thread. The dominant reaction is self-recognition from women who identify with the line about getting through everything alone, and a large share go further and disclose real circumstances — unemployment at 28, feeling isolated in a crowd, actively fighting to keep going. A second cluster addresses Goy directly and wishes her a year where she no longer has to get through things by herself, with several openly backing her new relationship. Viewers also treat the collaboration itself as a milestone they had been waiting for, and note that her voice now reads as a singer's rather than an actress who sings. The channel is running a pinned UGC campaign on the same thread — comment here or post with the sound on TikTok to win a signed copy of her book or channel pyjamas.

audience_signals: A cross-platform activation is already running here — the pinned comment routes YouTube commenters to post with the sound on TikTok for prizes, which is the clearest existing bridge between the two platforms
The subject matter (menstrual-cycle emotional vulnerability) is rare, ownable, and unlocks unusually personal disclosure — commenters share unemployment and loneliness, not just song praise
The audience tracks her vocal progression release by release, so the discography narrative itself is an asset to keep telling
Existing merchandise is visible in the thread — a signed book (THE TWENTIES' ACHE) and channel pyjamas — so a product line exists to build on
Collaborations the audience has already asked for convert best; this one was described as long-awaited before it happened
Comment sentiment is more mixed than other music posts because crying is the intended response — treat 'mixed' here as engagement, not dissatisfaction
content_requests: A live version of the duet
Keep releasing at this pace — no dislikes across her catalogue so far
Push the track past a million views
